premise: Woodpecker drums and drums, and Acorn and Pinecone wonder who he's talking to; nobody answers, but Acorn says "once more!" — and when he taps one more time, far away, another drum answers.
inspiration: The echo motif of folk tales (the voice that calls back from far away) and the folk-tale third try, turned: the answer isn't an echo but a real friend, and it comes because Woodpecker keeps calling.
lesson: Keep calling out; a friend may be listening.

en-US.title: Woodpecker Drums Hello
en-US.text: [excited] {woodpecker:enter} {woodpecker:go to trunks} Woodpecker clung to the bark of the big tree {woodpecker:live drum} {sfx:drum} and drummed. Rat-a-tat-TAT! Along walked little {acorn:enter} Acorn, and {pinecone:enter} {pinecone:go to acorn} Pinecone came rolling after her. {acorn:face surprised} [curious] "Who are you talking to?" asked Acorn. {woodpecker:face sad} "A friend I haven't met yet," said Woodpecker. "Somewhere far away." He {woodpecker:live tap hold} tapped again, and listened. [whispers] Nothing. {pinecone:face sad} Nothing at all. {acorn:face sad} Acorn wanted to help. "Once more!" she said, and she {acorn:live wish hold} closed her eyes tight and wished. Pinecone {pinecone:live open} opened all her scales, as if every one of them could listen. {woodpecker:live tap resume} So Woodpecker tapped one more time. {sfx:far-drum solo} Far, far away, someone drummed back! {acorn:live wish resume} Acorn's eyes popped open. {pinecone:face surprised} [gasps] "Did you hear that?" {woodpecker:face happy} "Rat-a-tat, hello!" drummed Woodpecker. "Rat-a-tat, hello, hello!" drummed the friend far away. {acorn:face happy} {acorn:hop x2} {pinecone:face happy} {pinecone:live bounce} Acorn and Pinecone bounced for joy. [happily] A brand-new friend… and they hadn't even met yet.

es-ES.title: El tambor de Carpintero
es-ES.text: [excited] {woodpecker:enter} {woodpecker:go to trunks} Pájaro carpintero se agarró a la corteza del árbol grande {woodpecker:live drum} {sfx:drum} y tamborileó. ¡Ra-ta-ta-TÁ! Por allí llegó la pequeña {acorn:enter} Bellota, y detrás, rodando, {pinecone:enter} {pinecone:go to acorn} Piña. {acorn:face surprised} [curious] —¿Con quién hablas? —preguntó Bellota. {woodpecker:face sad} —Con un amigo al que aún no conozco —dijo Carpintero—. Uno que vive lejos. {woodpecker:live tap hold} Tocó otra vez, y se quedó escuchando. [whispers] Nada. {pinecone:face sad} Nada de nada. {acorn:face sad} Bellota quería ayudar. —¡Otra vez! —dijo, y {acorn:live wish hold} cerró los ojos muy fuerte y pidió un deseo. Piña {pinecone:live open} abrió todas sus escamas, como si cada una pudiera escuchar. {woodpecker:live tap resume} Así que Carpintero tocó una vez más. {sfx:far-drum solo} ¡A lo lejos, muy lejos, alguien contestó! {acorn:live wish resume} Bellota abrió los ojos de par en par. {pinecone:face surprised} [gasps] —¿Lo habéis oído? {woodpecker:face happy} —Ra-ta-tá, ¡hola! —tamborileó Carpintero. —Ra-ta-tá, ¡hola, hola! —contestó el amigo lejano. {acorn:face happy} {acorn:hop x2} {pinecone:face happy} {pinecone:live bounce} Bellota y Piña dieron saltos de alegría. [happily] Un amigo nuevo… y todavía ni se conocían.
